items.where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P1
items.paragraph: Keep it simple. One thing you're doing, one anchor/image you're going with at first, one way of coming back, and feel free to set a tone (warm, bounded, directed, neutral witnessing, whatever) for yourself. If you're going to use metaphors just do one, and if you switch metaphors, do it in a way that's conscious.

items.before: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance
items.after: Using metaphors and imagery is entirely optional. You can use whatever form of signal shows up (feelings, rhythms, movements, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, lack of signal, whatever) but if you're using words, try to keep them related to whatever world you're creating. If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world. And when you're done, come back the other way. (You can borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness, but don't change who you are.)
published: Choose one purpose, one starting anchor or image, and a way back. Decide whether warmth, a firm boundary, direction, or neutral witnessing would help. Floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, colored light, and child dialogue do not all need to report for duty at once. Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.

After familiar runs, shorten a recording to the cues you still need, then try practicing without playback. Keep recordings when you enjoy them; independence means being able to guide yourself, not having to refuse help. The optional re-entry cue can shorten an already familiar induction.

published: Imagery is optional. A signal may arrive through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or no response at all. Keep the language in the world you chose: let a count mark something meaningful there, and reverse the journey when you finish. Borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness without replacing your identity.

Use Come all the way back, even when you ended early. Afterwards, write a few lines: what was there before; what I tried; what happened; what remains uncertain. Include a phrase, bodily signal, child’s need, protector’s concern, boundary, repair, or what not to force only when it actually appeared. You don’t owe the notebook a complete cast of characters.

items.where: Optional fractionation: practice coming back, P1
items.paragraph: Fractionation means returning toward ordinary awareness and then deciding whether to enter absorption again. Used openly, it teaches that trance has a door in both directions. At some point in time you can add this, but you must say you are doing it before doing it, so no answer can secretly mean “deeper.”

items.paragraph: For the no trance inner contact, I would do: Pacing: notice you can see, it's (day of the week), you have feet, you can read, you can write, etc. Suggestion: in your mind, ask one clear question and wait, but don't focus too hard. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous signal: write whatever you get (a word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence) without interpreting it as proof. Deepener: none (full alertness isn't a lesser version). Handoff: have your adult self answer the question in whatever way is appropriate, preferably by writing or doing. Integration/exit: reality test the signal and do one small thing based on it. Since you didn't go into trance, just close the exercise and carry on with your day.

items.after: Appendix K: Sources and further reading
published: The induction and inner meeting bring you to a place where you can listen. From here, learn to answer what happens instead of reciting a speech that has already decided what every part will say. Read these examples before practicing, then put the screen aside.

Observable pacing: Keep the eyes open, name the room and day, feel the feet, and read or write in ordinary awareness. Invitation: Ask one clear question and wait without narrowing attention further. Genuine choice: Answer, write “unsure,” rest, change the question, seek another person’s view, or stop. Autonomous signal: Record a word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence without interpreting it as proof. Deepener: None. Full alertness is not an inferior version of the practice. Handoff: Let the internal adult respond in writing or through one practical choice. Integration and exit: Reality-test the signal and do one small action. Because no altered state was cultivated, simply close the exercise and continue the day.

last_try.version: Autonomous signal: write down what you get, whether that's a word, a sensation, an impulse, an objection, or silence, and don't take it as proof. Deepener: none. Doing the inner contact fully alert doesn't make it a lesser version. Handoff: have your adult self answer the question however makes sense, ideally by writing something or doing something. Integration/exit: reality test the signal, then act on it in one small way. You didn't go into trance, so just close the exercise and get on with your day.
